verses.1:1: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, who reigned in Israel:
verses.1:2: to know wisdom and instruction, and to perceive words of prudence,
verses.1:3: and to receive subtleties of speech, to understand true righteousness, and to direct judgment aright;
verses.1:4: to give shrewdness to the innocent, and to a young lad both perception and discretion.
verses.1:5: For having heard these things, a wise man shall become wiser, and the discerning man shall acquire guidance,
verses.1:6: and he shall understand a parable and an obscure saying, both the utterances of the wise and riddles.
verses.1:7: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of God, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it; piety toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly shall despise wisdom and instruction.
verses.1:8: Hear, son, the instruction of your father, and do not cast away the ordinances of your mother;
verses.1:9: for you shall receive a crown of graces upon your head, and a golden chain about your neck.
verses.1:10: Son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray, nor consent
verses.1:11: if they urge you, saying, "Come with us, share in bloodshed, and let us unjustly hide a righteous man in the earth;
verses.1:12: let us swallow him up alive like Hades, and remove his remembrance from the earth;
verses.1:13: let us seize his costly wealth, and fill our houses with spoils;
verses.1:14: cast your lot among us, let us all acquire a common purse, and let there be one pouch for us."
verses.1:15: Do not walk in the way with them, but turn your foot aside from their paths;
verses.1:17: for nets are not spread out unjustly for winged creatures.
verses.1:18: For those very ones who partake of murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
verses.1:19: These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds; for by ungodliness they take away their own life.
verses.1:20: Wisdom is praised in the thoroughfares, and in the broad squares she speaks with boldness;
verses.1:21: on the tops of the walls she is proclaimed, at the gates of rulers she takes her seat, and at the gates of the city she boldly says:
verses.1:22: "For as long as the innocent hold fast to righteousness, they shall not be put to shame; but the foolish, being lovers of insolence, have become ungodly and hated perception,
verses.1:23: and have become liable to reproofs. Behold, I will pour forth to you an utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word.
verses.1:24: Because I called and you did not heed, and I extended words and you paid no attention,
verses.1:25: but you made my counsels void and disobeyed my reproofs,
verses.1:26: therefore I also will laugh at your destruction, and I will exult when ruin comes upon you,
verses.1:27: and when tumult arrives upon you suddenly, and overthrow is at hand like a tempest, and when affliction and siege come upon you, or when ruin comes upon you.
verses.1:28: For it shall come to pass that when you call upon me, I will not listen to you; wicked men shall seek me, and shall not find me.
verses.1:29: For they hated wisdom, and did not choose the word of the Lord;
verses.1:30: neither were they willing to attend to my counsels, but they derided my reproofs.
verses.1:31: Therefore they shall eat the fruits of their own way, and shall be filled with their own ungodliness;
verses.1:32: for because they wronged the simple, they shall be slain, and scrutiny shall destroy the ungodly.
verses.1:33: But he who listens to me shall dwell in hope, and shall rest without fear from every evil."
verses.2:1: Son, if you receive the utterance of my commandment and hide it within yourself,
verses.2:2: your ear shall heed wisdom, and you shall incline your heart to understanding, and you shall apply it to the admonition of your son.
verses.2:3: For if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding,
verses.2:4: and if you seek her as silver and search thoroughly for her as for treasures,
verses.2:5: then you shall understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.
verses.2:6: For the Lord gives wisdom, and from His countenance come knowledge and understanding;
verses.2:7: and He stores up salvation for those who walk uprightly; He shall shield their journey
verses.2:8: so as to guard the ways of righteous ordinances, and He shall preserve the way of those who revere Him.
verses.2:9: Then you shall understand righteousness and judgment, and you shall direct aright all good paths.
verses.2:10: For if wisdom enters into your mind, and perception seems good to your soul,
verses.2:11: good counsel shall guard you, and holy discretion shall keep you,
verses.2:12: that it may deliver you from an evil way, and from a man who speaks nothing trustworthy.
verses.2:13: O those who forsake straight ways to walk in ways of darkness,
verses.2:14: who delight in evil things and rejoice in wicked perversity,
verses.2:15: whose paths are crooked and whose courses are winding,
verses.2:16: so as to make you far from a straight way and estranged from righteous judgment. Son, do not let evil counsel overtake you,
verses.2:17: which forsakes the teaching of youth and has forgotten the divine covenant.
verses.2:18: For it has set its house beside death, and its tracks beside Hades with the earthborn;
verses.2:19: none of those who walk in it shall return, nor shall they attain straight paths; for they are not overtaken by the years of life.
verses.2:20: For if they had walked in good paths, they would have found the paths of righteousness smooth.
verses.2:21: For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the holy shall remain in it;
verses.2:22: the ways of the ungodly shall perish from the land, and the lawless shall be driven out from it.
verses.3:1: Son, do not forget my statutes, but let your heart keep my words;
verses.3:2: for they shall add to you length of lifetime and years of life and peace.
verses.3:3: Do not let deeds of mercy and faithfulness forsake you, but bind them upon your neck, and you shall find favor;
verses.3:4: and take thought for honorable things before the Lord and men.
verses.3:5: Be confident in God with your whole heart, and do not exalt yourself upon your own wisdom;
verses.3:6: in all your ways acknowledge her, so that she may cut your paths straight.
verses.3:7: Do not be wise in your own judgment, but fear God and turn away from all evil;
verses.3:8: then there shall be healing for your body and care for your bones.
verses.3:9: Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer to Him firstfruits from your fruits of righteousness,
verses.3:10: so that your storehouses may be filled to abundance with grain, and your winepresses may gush forth with wine.
verses.3:11: Son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor grow faint when you are reproved by Him;
verses.3:12: for whom the Lord loves He reproves, and He scourges every son whom He receives.
verses.3:13: Blessed is the man who has found wisdom, and the mortal who has seen understanding.
verses.3:14: For it is better to trade in her than in treasures of gold and silver.
verses.3:15: And she is more precious than costly stones; nothing evil shall oppose her. She is well known to all who draw near to her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
verses.3:16: For length of lifetime and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are wealth and glory; out of her mouth righteousness goes forth, and she bears law and mercy upon her tongue.
verses.3:17: Her ways are fair ways, and all her paths are in peace;
verses.3:18: she is a tree of life to all who hold fast to her, and to those who lean upon her as upon the Lord.
verses.3:19: God by wisdom founded the earth, and by understanding He prepared the heavens;
verses.3:20: by perception the deeps broke open, and the clouds poured forth dews.
verses.3:21: Son, do not slip away, but keep my counsel and insight,
verses.3:22: so that your soul may live, and grace may be around your neck. And there shall be healing for your flesh and care for your bones,
verses.3:23: that you may walk confidently in peace in all your ways, and your foot shall by no means stumble.
verses.3:24: For if you sit down, you shall be fearless, and if you sleep, you shall slumber sweetly;
verses.3:25: and you shall not fear terror when it comes, nor the onslaughts of the ungodly approaching;
verses.3:26: for the Lord shall be over all your ways, and He shall steady your foot so that you may not be shaken.
verses.3:27: Do not refrain from doing good to the needy, whenever your hand is able to help.
verses.3:28: Do not say, "Go back and come again, tomorrow I will give," when you are able to do good; for you do not know what the coming day shall bring forth.
verses.3:29: Do not devise evil things against your friend, who dwells beside you and trusts in you.
verses.3:30: Do not be hostile toward a man without cause, lest he do some evil to you.
verses.3:31: Do not acquire the reproaches of wicked men, nor envy their ways.
verses.3:32: For every lawless man is unclean before the Lord, and he does not sit in council among the righteous.
verses.3:33: The curse of God is in the houses of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed.
verses.3:34: The Lord opposes the proud, but to the humble He gives grace.
verses.3:35: The wise shall inherit glory, but the ungodly have exalted dishonor.
verses.4:1: Hear, children, the discipline of a father, and give heed to know insight.
verses.4:2: For I bestow upon you a good gift; do not forsake my law.
verses.4:3: For I also was a son obedient to a father, and beloved in the presence of a mother,
verses.4:4: who spoke and taught me, "Let our word be firmly fixed in your heart; keep commandments,
verses.4:5: do not forget, nor disregard the utterance of my mouth,
verses.4:6: nor forsake her, and she shall uphold you; love her ardently, and she shall guard you.
verses.4:8: Fence her about, and she shall exalt you; honor her, so that she may embrace you,
verses.4:9: that she may give to your head a crown of graces, and with a crown of delight she may shield you."
verses.4:10: Hear, son, and receive my words, and the years of your life shall be multiplied, so that many paths of living may be yours.
verses.4:11: For I teach you ways of wisdom, and I lead you onto straight paths.
verses.4:12: For if you walk, your steps shall not be hemmed in; and if you run, you shall not grow weary.
verses.4:13: Take hold of my discipline, do not let it go, but guard it for yourself for your life.
verses.4:14: Do not enter upon the ways of the ungodly, nor envy the ways of the lawless;
verses.4:15: in whatever place they encamp, do not go there, but turn away from them and pass by.
verses.4:16: For they shall by no means slumber unless they do evil; their sleep has been taken away, and they do not sleep;
verses.4:17: for these feed upon the food of ungodliness, and with lawless wine they grow drunk.
verses.4:18: But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they advance and give light until the day is established.
verses.4:19: But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.
verses.4:20: Son, give heed to my utterance, and incline your ear to my words,
verses.4:21: so that your springs may not fail you; guard them in your heart;
verses.4:22: for it is life to those who find it, and healing to all flesh.
verses.4:23: With all vigilance guard your heart, for from these are the issues of life.
verses.4:24: Remove from yourself a crooked mouth, and thrust unjust lips far away from you.
verses.4:25: Let your eyes look upon what is straight, and let your eyelids incline toward what is righteous.
verses.4:26: Make straight courses for your feet, and guide your ways straight.
verses.4:27: Do not turn aside to the right or to the left, but turn your foot away from an evil way. For God knows the ways on the right, but those on the left are crooked; and He Himself shall make your courses straight, and shall lead your journeys forward in peace.
verses.5:1: Son, give heed to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my words,
verses.5:2: that you may keep good understanding; and the discernment of my lips commands you.
verses.5:3: Do not give heed to a worthless woman; for honey drips from the lips of a harlot woman, who for a season makes your throat smooth;
verses.5:4: yet afterward you shall find it more bitter than gall, and sharper than a two-edged sword.
verses.5:5: For the feet of folly lead down those who associate with her with death into Hades, and her footsteps are not firmly established;
verses.5:6: for she does not walk in the ways of life, and her paths are slippery and not easily known.
verses.5:7: Now therefore, son, hear me, and do not make my words of no effect.
verses.5:8: Make your way far from her; do not draw near to the doors of her houses,
verses.5:9: lest you surrender your life to others, and your living to the merciless;
verses.5:10: lest strangers be filled with your strength, and your labors enter into the houses of strangers;
verses.5:11: and you shall feel remorse at the last, when the flesh of your body is worn away,
verses.5:12: and you shall say, "How I hated instruction, and my heart turned aside from reproofs;
verses.5:13: I did not listen to the voice of him who instructed me and taught me, nor did I incline my ear;
verses.5:14: I was almost in all evil in the midst of the assembly and congregation."
verses.5:15: Drink waters from your own vessels, and from the spring of your own wells.
verses.5:16: Do not let waters overflow for you from your spring, but let your waters flow out into your own streets;
verses.5:17: let them belong to you alone, and let no stranger share with you.
verses.5:18: Let your spring of water be your own, and rejoice with the wife of your youth.
verses.5:19: Let a doe of friendship and a colt of your graces keep company with you, and let your own wife lead you and be with you at all times; for walking continually in her friendship, you shall be greatly multiplied.
verses.5:20: Do not be much with a strange woman, nor come into the embrace of her who is not your own;
verses.5:21: for the ways of a man are before the eyes of God, and He looks upon all his paths.
verses.5:22: Transgressions ensnare a man, and each one is tightly bound with the cords of his own sins.
verses.5:23: This man dies with the uninstructed; from the abundance of his own living he is cast out, and he perishes through folly.
verses.6:1: Son, if you become surety for your friend, you shall deliver your hand to an enemy.
verses.6:2: For a man's own lips are a strong snare to him, and he is caught by the lips of his own mouth.
verses.6:3: Do, son, what I command you, and deliver yourself; for you have come into the hands of evil men on account of your friend. Do not grow faint, and also stir up your friend for whom you became surety.
verses.6:4: Do not give sleep to your eyes, nor let your eyelids slumber,
verses.6:5: that you may be delivered like a gazelle from snares, and like a bird from a trap.
verses.6:6: Go to the ant, O sluggard, and emulate him when you see his ways, and become wiser than he;
verses.6:7: for though he has no farmland, nor has anyone to compel him, nor is under a master,
verses.6:8: he prepares his food in the summer, and makes an abundant store in the harvest. Or go to the bee and learn what a worker she is, and how noble a work she performs; whose labors kings and common people partake of for health, and she is desired by all and held in honor; though she is weak in strength, by honoring wisdom she has been exalted.
verses.6:9: How long, sluggard, do you lie down? And when will you rise from sleep?
verses.6:10: A little you sleep, and a little you sit, a short while you slumber, and a little you clasp your chest with your hands;
verses.6:11: then poverty comes upon you like an evil wayfarer, and want like a good runner. Yet if you are not slothful, your harvest shall come like a spring, and want shall flee away like a poor runner.
verses.6:12: A foolish and lawless man walks in ways that are not good;
verses.6:13: that same man winks with his eye, signals with his foot, and teaches with gestures of his fingers;
verses.6:14: with a perverse heart he devises evil things at all times; such a man stirs up tumults in a city.
verses.6:15: Therefore his destruction comes suddenly, a cutting off and an incurable shattering;
verses.6:16: because he rejoices in all things that God hates, and he is shattered because of uncleanness of soul:
verses.6:17: the eye of an insolent man, an unrighteous tongue, hands that shed the blood of a righteous man,
verses.6:18: and a heart devising evil thoughts, and feet hastening to do evil.
verses.6:19: An unrighteous witness kindles falsehoods, and sends disputes among brethren.
verses.6:20: Son, keep the laws of your father, and do not reject the ordinances of your mother;
verses.6:21: bind them upon your soul continually, and fasten them like a collar around your neck.
verses.6:22: Whenever you walk, bring it along, and let it be with you; and when you sleep, let it guard you, that when you awake it may converse with you.
verses.6:23: For the commandment of the law is a lamp, and the way of life and reproof and instruction are a light,
verses.6:24: to preserve you from a married woman, and from the slander of a strange tongue.
verses.6:25: Do not let desire for beauty overcome you, nor be ensnared by your eyes, nor be carried away by her eyelids.
verses.6:26: For the price of a harlot is as much as one loaf of bread, yet a woman hunts the precious souls of men.
verses.6:27: Will anyone bind fire in his bosom, and not burn up his garments?
verses.6:28: Or will anyone walk upon coals of fire, and not burn his feet?
verses.6:29: So is he who goes in to a married woman; he shall not be held guiltless, nor shall anyone who touches her.
verses.6:30: It is no wonder if someone is caught stealing, for he steals to fill his soul when he is hungry;
verses.6:31: yet if he is caught, he shall repay sevenfold, and by giving all his possessions he shall deliver himself;
verses.6:32: but the adulterer, through lack of understanding, procures destruction for his own soul;
verses.6:33: he endures both pains and dishonors, and his reproach shall not be blotted out forever.
verses.6:34: For the wrath of her husband is full of jealousy; he shall not spare in the day of judgment.
verses.6:35: He will not exchange his enmity for any ransom, nor will he be reconciled by many gifts.
verses.7:1: Son, keep my words, and hide my commandments within yourself; son, honor the Lord and you shall be strong, and besides Him do not fear another.
verses.7:2: Guard my commandments and you shall live, and my words as the pupils of your eyes;
verses.7:3: bind them around your fingers, and inscribe them upon the breadth of your heart.
verses.7:4: Say that wisdom is your sister, and acquire prudence as a familiar friend for yourself,
verses.7:5: that she may guard you from a strange and wicked woman, if she should assail you with words spoken for favor.
verses.7:6: For peering down from a window out of her house into the streets,
verses.7:7: whomever she sees among the foolish children, a young man devoid of understanding,
verses.7:8: passing along beside the corner in the passageways of her houses, and speaking
verses.7:9: in the evening darkness, whenever there is the stillness of night and thick gloom,
verses.7:10: then the woman meets him, having the appearance of a harlot, she who causes the hearts of young men to take flight.
verses.7:11: Now she is restless and dissolute, and her feet do not remain still at home;
verses.7:12: for at one time she wanders outside, and at another time she lies in ambush in the streets at every corner.
verses.7:13: Then taking hold of him, she kissed him, and with a shameless countenance she spoke to him:
verses.7:14: "I have a peace offering; today I fulfill my vows.
verses.7:15: Because of this I came out to meet you; longing for your face, I have found you.
verses.7:16: I have strung my bed with cords, and I have spread it with double-woven tapestries from Egypt;
verses.7:17: I have sprinkled my couch with saffron, and my house with cinnamon;
verses.7:18: come, and let us enjoy love until dawn; come, and let us entwine ourselves in passion.
verses.7:19: For my husband is not at home, but he has gone on a long journey,
verses.7:20: having taken a bundle of silver in his hand; after many days he will return to his house."
verses.7:21: So she led him astray with much conversation, and with the snares from her lips she drove him off course;
verses.7:22: and he followed after her, easily beguiled, just as an ox is led to the slaughter, and as a dog to bonds,
verses.7:23: or like a stag struck in the liver by an arrow; and he hastens like a bird into a trap, not knowing that he runs at the cost of his life.
verses.7:24: Now therefore, son, listen to me, and pay heed to the words of my mouth.
verses.7:25: Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways;
verses.7:26: for she has wounded and cast down many, and countless are those whom she has slain;
verses.7:27: her house is the ways of Hades, leading down to the inner chambers of death.
verses.8:1: You shall proclaim wisdom, that prudence may obey you.
verses.8:2: For she is upon the lofty heights, and she stands in the midst of the paths;
verses.8:3: for beside the gates of rulers she sits, and at the entrances she is praised:
verses.8:4: "To you, O men, I call, and I send forth my voice to the sons of men.
verses.8:5: Understand shrewdness, you innocent ones, and you who are uninstructed, lay up a heart within yourselves.
verses.8:6: Listen to me, for I will speak noble things, and from my lips I will bring forth what is right.
verses.8:7: For my throat shall meditate upon truth, and lying lips are an abomination before me;
verses.8:8: all the words of my mouth are with righteousness; nothing in them is crooked or twisted;
verses.8:9: all of them are plain before those who understand, and upright to those who find knowledge.
verses.8:10: Receive instruction and not silver, and knowledge rather than tested gold;
verses.8:11: for wisdom is better than costly stones, and no precious thing is worthy of her.
verses.8:12: I, wisdom, have made counsel my dwelling, and I have called upon knowledge and discretion; for wisdom is better than costly stones.
verses.8:13: The fear of the Lord hates unrighteousness, both insolence and arrogance and the ways of wicked men; and I have hated the perverted ways of evil men.
verses.8:14: Mine are counsel and security; mine is prudence, and mine is strength;
verses.8:15: by me kings reign, and rulers inscribe righteousness;
verses.8:16: by me great men are magnified, and sovereigns rule the earth by me.
verses.8:17: I love those who cherish me, and those who seek me shall find.
verses.8:18: Wealth and glory belong to me, even the possession of many things and righteousness.
verses.8:19: It is better to reap fruit from me than gold and precious stone, and my produce is better than choice silver.
verses.8:20: I walk in the ways of righteousness, and I move about in the midst of the paths of justice,
verses.8:21: that I may apportion substance to those who love me, and fill their treasuries with good things. If I declare to you the things that happen day by day, I will remember to recount the things from eternity.
verses.8:22: The Lord created me as the beginning of His ways for His works;
verses.8:23: before the age He founded me in the beginning, before He made the earth,
verses.8:24: and before He made the deeps, before the springs of the waters came forth,
verses.8:25: before the mountains were settled, and before all hills He begets me.
verses.8:26: The Lord made lands and uninhabited regions, and the inhabited heights of what lies beneath the heavens.
verses.8:27: When He was preparing the heaven, I was present with Him, and when He was setting apart His own throne upon the winds;
verses.8:28: and when He was making the clouds above strong, and when He was making secure the springs of what lies beneath heaven,
verses.8:29: and when He was making strong the foundations of the earth,
verses.8:30: I was beside Him, fitting things together; I was the one in whom He took delight, and day by day I rejoiced before His face at every season,
verses.8:31: when He was glad after bringing the inhabited world to completion, and rejoiced in the sons of men.
verses.8:32: Now therefore, son, listen to me.
verses.8:34: Blessed is the man who will listen to me, and the one who will guard my ways, keeping vigil at my doors day by day, watching over the doorposts of my entrances.
verses.8:35: For my goings forth are goings forth of life, and favor is prepared from the Lord.
verses.8:36: But those who sin against me act wickedly against their own souls, and those who hate me love death."
verses.9:1: Wisdom built a house for herself, and set up seven pillars;
verses.9:2: she slew her offerings, mixed her wine in a mixing bowl, and made ready her table.
verses.9:3: She sent forth her servants, calling together with a lofty proclamation to the mixing bowl, saying,
verses.9:4: "Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me," and to those who lack sense she said,
verses.9:5: "Come, eat of my loaves, and drink wine which I have mixed for you.
verses.9:6: Forsake foolishness, that you may reign forever, and seek prudence, and set understanding upright in knowledge."
verses.9:7: He who instructs evil men shall receive dishonor for himself, and he who reproves the ungodly man shall bring reproach upon himself.
verses.9:8: Do not reprove evil men, lest they hate you; reprove a wise man, and he will love you.
verses.9:9: Give an occasion to a wise man, and he will become wiser; impart knowledge to a righteous man, and he will increase in receiving.
verses.9:10: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of the holy ones is understanding; for to know the law belongs to a good mind.
verses.9:11: For in this manner you shall live a long time, and years of your life shall be added to you.
verses.9:12: Son, if you become wise for yourself, you shall also be wise for your neighbors; but if you turn out evil, you alone shall endure evils. He who relies upon falsehoods, this man shepherds winds, and the same shall pursue flying birds; for he has forsaken the ways of his own vineyard, and has strayed from the tracks of his own field; he journeys through a waterless wilderness and a land appointed to parched places, and with his hands he gathers barrenness.
verses.9:13: A foolish and brazen woman comes to lack a morsel of bread, she who does not know shame;
verses.9:14: she sat at the doors of her own house upon a seat, openly in the streets,
verses.9:15: calling to those who pass by and go straight along their ways,
verses.9:16: "Whoever among you is most foolish, let him turn aside to me; and to those who lack prudence I give this charge, saying,
verses.9:17: 'Gladly partake of hidden loaves, and of sweet stolen water.'"
verses.9:18: But he does not know that the earthborn perish with her, and he meets the trap of Hades. Rather, leap away, do not linger in the place, nor fix your eye upon her; for thus you shall pass across strange water. Abstain from strange water, and do not drink from a strange fountain, that you may live a long time, and years of life may be added to you.
verses.10:1: A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
verses.10:2: Treasures shall not profit the lawless, but righteousness shall deliver from death.
verses.10:3: The Lord will not starve a righteous soul, but He will overturn the life of the ungodly.
verses.10:4: Poverty humbles a man, but the hands of the valiant make rich. A disciplined son shall be wise, and he shall use the fool as a servant.
verses.10:5: A prudent son is saved from the scorching heat, but a lawless son becomes wind-blighted in the harvest.
verses.10:6: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of a righteous man, but untimely mourning shall cover the mouth of the ungodly.
verses.10:7: The memory of the righteous is with praises, but the name of the ungodly man is extinguished.
verses.10:8: The wise in heart shall receive commandments, but he who is unrestrained with his lips, going crookedly, shall be tripped up.
verses.10:9: He who walks with sincerity walks in confidence, but he who perverts his ways shall be known.
verses.10:10: He who winks with his eyes deceitfully gathers griefs for men, but he who reproves with boldness makes peace.
verses.10:11: A fountain of life is in the hand of a righteous man, but destruction shall cover the mouth of the ungodly man.
verses.10:12: Hatred stirs up strife, but friendship covers all who are not contentious;
verses.10:13: with a rod it strikes a senseless man.
verses.10:14: The wise shall conceal knowledge, but the mouth of the rash draws near to ruin.
verses.10:15: The possession of the rich is a fortified city, but the ruin of the ungodly is poverty.
verses.10:16: The works of the righteous produce life, but the fruits of the ungodly produce sins.
verses.10:17: Instruction keeps the righteous ways of life, but instruction left unreproved goes astray.
verses.10:18: Righteous lips cover enmity, but those who bring forth revilings are most foolish.
verses.10:19: From much speaking you shall not escape sin, but by sparing your lips you shall be prudent.
verses.10:20: The tongue of a righteous man is silver refined by fire, but the heart of the ungodly man shall fail.
verses.10:21: The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but fools come to their end in want.
verses.10:22: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of a righteous man; it makes rich, and grief shall by no means be added to it in the heart.
verses.10:23: With laughter a fool practices evil, but wisdom brings forth prudence for a man.
verses.10:24: The ungodly man is swept about in destruction, but the desire of a righteous man is acceptable.
verses.10:25: When a tempest passes by, the ungodly man vanishes away, but the righteous man turns aside and is saved forever.
verses.10:26: As an unripe grape is harmful to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is lawlessness to those who practice it.
verses.10:27: The fear of the Lord adds days, but the years of the ungodly shall be diminished.
verses.10:28: Gladness abides long with the righteous, but the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
verses.10:29: The fear of the Lord is a stronghold for the devout, but ruin for those who work evil.
verses.10:30: A righteous man shall never give way, but the ungodly shall not dwell in the land.
verses.10:31: The mouth of a righteous man distills wisdom, but the tongue of an unrighteous man shall utterly perish.
verses.10:32: The lips of righteous men distill graces, but the mouth of the ungodly turns aside.
verses.11:1: Deceitful scales are an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is acceptable to Him.
verses.11:2: Wherever arrogance enters, there also is dishonor; but the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom.
verses.11:3: When a righteous man dies, he leaves regret behind, but the destruction of the ungodly is swift and rejoiced over.
verses.11:5: Righteousness cuts straight blameless ways, but ungodliness falls into unrighteousness.
verses.11:6: The righteousness of upright men delivers them, but the lawless are caught in their own destruction.
verses.11:7: When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boast of the ungodly perishes.
verses.11:8: A righteous man escapes from the snare, and in his place the ungodly man is delivered up.
verses.11:9: In the mouth of the ungodly is a snare for citizens, but the discernment of the righteous is prosperous.
verses.11:10: Through the good things of the righteous a city prospers,
verses.11:11: but by the mouths of the ungodly it is overthrown.
verses.11:12: He who is lacking in understanding mocks citizens, but a prudent man keeps silence.
verses.11:13: A double-tongued man reveals counsels in the assembly, but one faithful in spirit conceals matters.
verses.11:14: Those who have no guidance fall like leaves, but safety is in much counsel.
verses.11:15: A wicked man does harm whenever he associates with a righteous man, and he hates the sound of security.
verses.11:16: A gracious woman raises up glory for her husband, but a woman who hates righteous things is a throne of dishonor. The slothful become destitute of wealth, while the valiant are supported by wealth.
verses.11:17: A merciful man does good to his own soul, but the merciless man destroys his own body.
verses.11:18: An ungodly man performs unrighteous works, but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth.
verses.11:19: A righteous son is born for life, but the pursuit of an ungodly man leads to death.
verses.11:20: Perverse ways are an abomination to the Lord, but all who are blameless in their ways are acceptable to Him.
verses.11:21: He who joins hands unjustly shall not go unpunished, but he who sows righteousness shall receive a faithful reward.
verses.11:22: Like an earring in a swine's snout, so is beauty to an ill-minded woman.
verses.11:23: Every desire of the righteous is good, but the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
verses.11:24: There are those who sow their own possessions and gain more; and there are also those who gather in and are diminished.
verses.11:25: Every sincere soul is blessed, but a wrathful man is unseemly.
verses.11:26: He who withholds grain, may he leave it behind to the nations; but blessing is upon the head of him who shares it.
verses.11:27: He who devises good things seeks good favor, but as for him who earnestly seeks evil, it shall overtake him.
verses.11:28: He who trusts in wealth, he shall fall, but he who upholds the righteous, he shall flourish.
verses.11:29: He who does not deal considerately with his own household shall inherit wind, and a fool shall serve a prudent man.
verses.11:30: From the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life, but the souls of the lawless are taken away before their time.
verses.11:31: If the righteous man is saved with difficulty, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?
verses.12:1: He who loves discipline loves discernment, but he who hates reproofs is a fool.
verses.12:2: Better is he who has found favor with the Lord, but a lawless man shall be passed over in silence.
verses.12:3: A man shall not prosper by what is lawless, but the roots of the righteous shall not be uprooted.
verses.12:4: A valiant woman is a crown to her husband; but like a worm in wood, so a woman who works evil destroys a husband.
verses.12:5: The thoughts of the righteous are judgments, but the ungodly direct deceits.
verses.12:6: The words of the ungodly are deceitful, but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
verses.12:7: Wherever he turns, an ungodly man vanishes away, but the houses of the righteous endure.
verses.12:8: The mouth of a discerning man is praised by a man, but the dull-hearted is mocked.
verses.12:9: Better is a man in dishonor who serves himself than one who puts honor upon himself and lacks bread.
verses.12:10: A righteous man has compassion on the lives of his livestock, but the tender affections of the ungodly are merciless.
verses.12:11: He who tills his own land shall be filled with bread, but those who pursue vain things are lacking in understanding. He who finds pleasure in lingering over wine shall leave dishonor in his own strongholds.
verses.12:12: The desires of the ungodly are evil, but the roots of the godly are in strongholds.
verses.12:13: Through the sin of his lips a sinner falls into snares, but a righteous man escapes from them. He whose look is gentle shall receive mercy, but he who confronts others in the gates shall afflict souls.
verses.12:14: From the fruits of the mouth a man's soul shall be filled with good things, and the recompense of his lips shall be given to him.
verses.12:15: The ways of fools are right before them, but a wise man heeds counsel.
verses.12:16: A fool declares his wrath the very same day, but a prudent man conceals his own dishonor.
verses.12:17: A righteous man declares manifest faithfulness, but the witness of the unrighteous is deceitful.
verses.12:18: There are those whose words wound like swords, but the tongues of the wise bring healing.
verses.12:19: Truthful lips establish testimony, but a hasty witness has an unrighteous tongue.
verses.12:20: Deceit is in the heart of him who devises evil, but those who desire peace shall rejoice.
verses.12:21: Nothing unrighteous shall please the righteous man, but the ungodly shall be filled with evils.
verses.12:22: False lips are an abomination to the Lord, but he who performs faithful deeds is acceptable with Him.
verses.12:23: An understanding man is a throne of discernment, but the heart of fools shall meet with curses.
verses.12:24: The hand of the chosen shall rule with ease, but the deceitful shall be for plunder.
verses.12:25: A fearful word troubles the heart of a righteous man, but a good message makes him glad.
verses.12:26: A discerning righteous man shall be a friend to himself, but evils shall pursue those who sin, and the way of the ungodly shall lead them astray.
verses.12:27: A deceitful man shall not catch prey, but a pure man is a precious possession.
verses.12:28: In the ways of righteousness is life, but the ways of those who hold grudges lead to death.
verses.13:1: A prudent son is obedient to his father, but a disobedient son is in destruction.
verses.13:2: From the fruits of righteousness a good man shall eat, but the souls of the lawless shall perish before their time.
verses.13:3: He who guards his own mouth preserves his own soul, but he who is rash with his lips shall bring terror upon himself.
verses.13:4: Every idle man is full of desires, but the hands of the valiant are in diligence.
verses.13:5: A righteous man hates an unjust word, but an ungodly man is put to shame and shall have no boldness.
verses.13:7: There are those who make themselves rich, yet have nothing; and there are those who humble themselves in great wealth.
verses.13:8: The ransom of a man's soul is his own wealth, but a poor man does not endure a threat.
verses.13:9: Light belongs to the righteous continually, but the light of the ungodly is extinguished. Deceitful souls go astray in sins, but the righteous have compassion and show mercy.
verses.13:10: An evil man commits evil deeds with insolence, but those who are judges of themselves are wise.
verses.13:11: Substance hurriedly gained with lawlessness diminishes, but he who gathers for himself with godliness shall be multiplied; a righteous man has compassion and lends.
verses.13:12: Better is he who helps from the heart those who are beginning than he who promises and leads into hope; for a good desire is a tree of life.
verses.13:13: He who despises a matter shall be despised by it; but he who fears a commandment, that man is sound in health. For a deceitful son there shall be nothing good; but for a wise servant his deeds shall prosper, and his way shall be directed straight.
verses.13:14: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, but the senseless man shall die by a snare.
verses.13:15: Good understanding gives favor, and to know the law belongs to a good mind, but the ways of despisers are in destruction.
verses.13:16: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but the fool spreads open his own wickedness.
verses.13:17: A rash king shall fall into evils, but a wise messenger shall deliver him.
verses.13:18: Instruction takes away poverty and dishonor, and he who keeps reproofs shall be honored.
verses.13:19: The desires of the godly sweeten the soul, but the works of the ungodly are far from knowledge.
verses.13:20: By walking with the wise you shall be wise, but he who walks with fools shall be known.
verses.13:21: Evils shall pursue those who sin, but good things shall overtake the righteous.
verses.13:22: A good man shall leave an inheritance to his sons' sons, and the wealth of the ungodly is stored up for the righteous.
verses.13:23: The righteous shall spend many years in wealth, but the unjust shall perish swiftly.
verses.13:24: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.
verses.13:25: A righteous man eats and fills his soul, but the souls of the ungodly are in want.
verses.14:1: Wise women build houses, but the foolish woman demolishes hers with her hands.
verses.14:2: He who walks uprightly fears the Lord, but he who is crooked in his ways shall be dishonored.
verses.14:3: Out of the mouth of fools comes a rod of insolence, but the lips of the wise guard them.
verses.14:4: Where there are no oxen, the mangers are clean; but where there are abundant crops, the strength of an ox is evident.
verses.14:5: A faithful witness does not lie, but an unjust witness kindles falsehoods.
verses.14:6: You shall seek wisdom among evil men and shall not find it, but discernment is readily found among the prudent.
verses.14:7: All things are contrary to a foolish man, but wise lips are weapons of discernment.
verses.14:8: The wisdom of the prudent shall discern their ways, but the senselessness of fools is in error.
verses.14:9: The houses of the lawless shall owe purification, but the houses of the righteous are acceptable.
verses.14:10: A man's heart is sensitive, and his soul is sorrowful; yet when he rejoices, he does not mingle with insolence.
verses.14:11: The houses of the ungodly shall be destroyed, but the tents of the upright shall stand.
verses.14:12: There is a way that seems right among men, but its end comes to the depths of Hades.
verses.14:13: In times of gladness sorrow is not mingled, yet the end of joy comes to mourning.
verses.14:14: A presumptuous-hearted man shall be filled with his own ways, and a good man from his own thoughts.
verses.14:15: The guileless man believes every word, but the prudent man comes to repentance.
verses.14:16: A wise man fears and turns aside from evil, but the fool, trusting in himself, mingles with the lawless.
verses.14:17: A quick-tempered man acts without counsel, but a prudent man endures many things.
verses.14:18: Fools shall share wickedness as their portion, but the prudent shall lay hold of discernment.
verses.14:19: Evil men shall slip before the good, and the ungodly shall wait upon the doors of the righteous.
verses.14:20: Friends shall hate poor friends, but the friends of the rich are many.
verses.14:21: He who dishonors the needy sins, but he who shows mercy to the poor is blessed.
verses.14:22: Those who go astray craft evil, but the good craft mercy and truth; craftsmen of evil do not know mercy and faithfulness, but deeds of mercy and faithfulness dwell with good craftsmen.
verses.14:23: In everyone who takes diligent care there is abundance, but the pleasure-loving and unfeeling man shall be in want.
verses.14:24: The crown of the wise is a prudent man, but the pastime of fools is evil.
verses.14:25: A faithful witness shall deliver a soul from evils, but a deceitful man kindles falsehoods.
verses.14:26: In the fear of the Lord is a hope of strength, and for His children He leaves a support.
verses.14:27: The ordinance of the Lord is a fountain of life, and it causes one to turn aside from the snare of death.
verses.14:28: In a numerous nation is the glory of a king, but in the failing of a people is the ruin of a ruler.
verses.14:29: A longsuffering man is great in prudence, but the impatient man is a mighty fool.
verses.14:30: A gentle-spirited man is a physician of the heart, but a sensitive heart is a moth to the bones.
verses.14:31: He who oppresses the needy provokes the One who made him, but he who honors Him shows mercy to the poor.
verses.14:32: In his wickedness the ungodly man shall be thrust away, but he who trusts in his own holiness is righteous.
verses.14:33: In the good heart of a man is wisdom, but in the heart of fools it is not discerned.
verses.14:34: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sins diminish tribes.
verses.14:35: An understanding servant is acceptable to a king, and by his own resourcefulness he takes away dishonor.
verses.15:1: Wrath destroys even the prudent, but a submissive answer turns away fury, while a grievous word stirs up wrath.
verses.15:2: The tongue of the wise knows good things, but the mouth of fools will declare evil.
verses.15:3: In every place are the eyes of the Lord; they keep watch over both the evil and the good.
verses.15:4: The healing of the tongue is a tree of life, and he who guards it shall be filled with spirit.
verses.15:6: A fool mocks a father's instruction, but he who keeps commandments is more shrewd. In abounding righteousness there is great strength, but the ungodly shall perish completely uprooted from the earth; in the houses of the righteous there is great strength, but the fruits of the ungodly shall perish.
verses.15:7: The lips of the wise are bound with discernment, but the hearts of fools are not secure.
verses.15:8: The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of those who walk uprightly are acceptable before Him.
verses.15:9: The ways of an ungodly man are an abomination to the Lord, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
verses.15:10: The discipline of the guileless is recognized by those who pass by, but those who hate reproofs die shamefully.
verses.15:11: Hades and destruction are manifest before the Lord; how could the hearts of men not be also?
verses.15:12: An undisciplined man will not love those who reprove him, nor will he keep company with the wise.
verses.15:13: When the heart rejoices, the countenance flourishes, but when it is in sorrows, it grows downcast.
verses.15:14: An upright heart seeks discernment, but the mouth of the undisciplined will know evil things.
verses.15:15: At all times the eyes of the wicked expect evil things, but the good shall abide in quietness continually.
verses.15:16: Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord than great treasures without fear.
verses.15:17: Better is hospitality with herbs in friendship and grace than a serving of calves with enmity.
verses.15:18: A wrathful man prepares strife, but a longsuffering man calms even that which is impending; a longsuffering man will quench disputes, while the ungodly man stirs them up all the more.
verses.15:19: The ways of the idle are strewn with thorns, but those of the valiant are worn smooth.
verses.15:20: A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son mocks his mother.
verses.15:21: The paths of a senseless man are lacking in understanding, but a prudent man walks directing his course aright.
verses.15:22: Those who do not honor councils postpone their plans, but in the hearts of those who take counsel, counsel abides.
verses.15:23: The wicked man will by no means heed it, nor will he speak anything timely and good for the community.
verses.15:24: The thoughts of an understanding man are ways of life, that turning aside from Hades he may be saved.
verses.15:25: The Lord tears down the houses of the arrogant, yet He establishes the boundary of a widow.
verses.15:26: An unrighteous thought is an abomination to the Lord, but the sayings of the pure are honorable.
verses.15:27: He who takes bribes utterly destroys himself, but he who hates the receiving of bribes is saved. By acts of mercy and faithfulness sins are cleansed away, and by the fear of the Lord everyone turns aside from evil.
verses.15:28: The hearts of the righteous meditate on faithfulness, but the mouth of the ungodly answers evil things. The ways of righteous men are acceptable before the Lord, and through them even enemies become friends.
verses.15:29: God is far removed from the ungodly, but He heeds the prayers of the righteous. Better is a small gain with righteousness than abundant revenues with unrighteousness. And let the heart of a man ponder righteous things, that his steps may be directed aright by God.
verses.15:30: An eye that beholds good things gladdens the heart, and a good report gives fatness to the bones.
verses.15:32: He who rejects instruction hates himself, but he who observes reproofs loves his own soul.
verses.15:33: The fear of God is instruction and wisdom, and the beginning of glory shall answer to it.
verses.16:2: All the works of the humble man are manifest before God, but the ungodly shall perish in an evil day.
verses.16:5: Everyone who is haughty in heart is unclean before God, and he who joins hand to hand unjustly shall not be held guiltless.
verses.16:7: The beginning of a good way is to do righteous things, and these are more acceptable before God than to offer sacrifices.
verses.16:8: He who seeks the Lord shall find knowledge with righteousness, and those who seek Him aright shall find peace.
verses.16:9: All the works of the Lord are with righteousness, and the ungodly man is reserved for an evil day.
verses.16:10: An oracle is upon the lips of a king, and in judgment his mouth shall by no means err.
verses.16:11: The turn of the scales is righteousness before the Lord, and His works are just weights.
verses.16:12: He who does evil is an abomination to a king, for with righteousness a throne of dominion is prepared.
verses.16:13: Righteous lips are acceptable to a king, and he loves upright words.
verses.16:14: The fury of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease it.
verses.16:15: In the light of life is the son of a king, and those acceptable to him are like a latter cloud.
verses.16:16: The nests of wisdom are more desirable than gold, and the nests of prudence are more desirable than silver.
verses.16:17: The paths of life turn aside from evils, and the ways of righteousness are length of life. He who receives instruction shall be among good things, and he who keeps reproofs shall be made wise. He who guards his own ways preserves his own soul, and he who loves his life will spare his mouth.
verses.16:18: Arrogance goes before ruin, and evil-mindedness before a fall.
verses.16:19: Better is a gentle-spirited man with humility than he who divides spoil with the arrogant.
verses.16:20: He who is understanding in affairs is a finder of good things, and he who trusts in God is most blessed.
verses.16:21: They call the wise and understanding worthless, yet those who are sweet in speech shall hear more.
verses.16:22: Insight is a fountain of life to those who possess it, but the instruction of fools is evil.
verses.16:23: The heart of a wise man will understand what comes from his own mouth, and upon his lips he will bear discernment.
verses.16:24: Good words are combs of honey, and its sweetness is healing for the soul.
verses.16:25: There are ways that seem upright to a man, yet their end looks toward the depth of Hades.
verses.16:26: A man in toils labors for himself and drives away his own destruction; the crooked man, however, bears destruction upon his own mouth.
verses.16:27: A foolish man digs up evils for himself, and upon his own lips he treasures up fire.
verses.16:28: A crooked man sends forth evils, and he will kindle a torch of deceit for the wicked, and he separates friends.
verses.16:29: A lawless man tempts friends and leads them away along ways that are not good.
verses.16:30: And fixing his eyes, he devises perverse things, and with his lips he decrees all evils; this man is a furnace of wickedness.
verses.16:31: Old age is a crown of glorying, and it is found in the ways of righteousness.
verses.16:32: Better is a longsuffering man than a mighty one, and he who masters wrath is better than one who captures a city.
verses.16:33: All things come into the laps of the unrighteous, yet all righteous things are from the Lord.
verses.17:1: Better is a morsel with delight in peace than a house of many good things and unjust sacrifices with strife.
verses.17:2: A discerning servant shall rule over foolish masters, and among brethren he shall divide portions.
verses.17:3: Just as silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so are chosen hearts before the Lord.
verses.17:4: An evil man listens to the tongue of transgressors, but a righteous man does not give heed to lying lips.
verses.17:5: He who mocks a poor man provokes Him who made him, and he who rejoices over one who is perishing shall not go unpunished; but he who shows compassion shall obtain mercy.
verses.17:6: Children's children are the crown of old men, and the boast of children is their fathers. To the faithful man belongs the whole world of wealth, but to the unfaithful man not even an obol.
verses.17:7: Faithful lips will not befit a fool, nor lying lips a righteous man.
verses.17:8: Instruction is a reward of graces to those who use it, and wherever one turns, he shall prosper.
verses.17:9: He who conceals offenses seeks friendship, but he who hates to conceal them separates friends and kindred.
verses.17:10: A threat crushes the heart of a prudent man, but a fool, though scourged, does not perceive it.
verses.17:11: Every evil man stirs up contentions, and the Lord shall send out a merciless messenger against him.
verses.17:12: Anxiety shall fall upon a discerning man, but fools shall devise evil things.
verses.17:13: He who repays evil for good—evil shall not be removed from his house.
verses.17:14: The beginning of righteousness gives authority to words, but sedition and strife go before want.
verses.17:15: He who judges the unrighteous man to be righteous, and the righteous man to be unrighteous, is unclean and abominable before God.
verses.17:16: For what purpose did wealth belong to a fool? For a senseless man will not be able to acquire wisdom. He who makes his own house lofty seeks ruin, and he who turns perversely from learning shall fall into evils.
verses.17:17: Let a friend be yours at every season, and let brethren be helpful in times of distress, for on account of this they are born.
verses.17:18: A foolish man claps his hands and rejoices in himself, as also does he who pledges surety for his own friends.
verses.17:19: A lover of sin rejoices in quarrels,
verses.17:20: and the hard-hearted man does not meet with good things. A man changeable in tongue shall fall into evils,
verses.17:21: and the heart of a fool is sorrow to him who possesses it. A father does not rejoice over an undisciplined son, but a prudent son gladdens his mother.
verses.17:22: A glad heart brings good health, but the bones of a sorrowful man dry up.
verses.17:23: The ways of him who unjustly takes gifts into his bosom do not prosper, and an ungodly man turns aside the paths of righteousness.
verses.17:24: The countenance of a wise man is discerning, but the eyes of the fool are upon the ends of the earth.
verses.17:25: A foolish son is anger to his father, and sorrow to her who bore him.
verses.17:26: To penalize a righteous man is not good, nor is it holy to plot against righteous rulers.
verses.17:27: He who refrains from uttering a harsh word is perceptive, and a longsuffering man is prudent.
verses.17:28: To a senseless man who inquires after wisdom, wisdom shall be reckoned, and he who makes himself mute shall seem to be prudent.
verses.18:1: A man who wishes to separate himself from friends seeks pretexts, and at every season he shall be subject to reproach.
verses.18:2: He who lacks understanding has no need of wisdom, for he is led rather by folly.
verses.18:3: Whenever an ungodly man comes into a depth of evils, he shows contempt, and dishonor and reproach come upon him.
verses.18:4: A word in the heart of a man is deep water, and a river and a fountain of life spring forth.
verses.18:5: To respect the person of an ungodly man is not good, nor is it holy to turn aside justice in judgment.
verses.18:6: The lips of a fool lead him into evils, and his bold mouth calls upon death.
verses.18:7: The mouth of a fool is destruction to him, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
verses.18:8: Fear casts down the slothful, and the souls of the effeminate shall hunger.
verses.18:9: He who does not heal himself in his works is a brother to him who ruins himself.
verses.18:10: From greatness of strength is the name of the Lord, and the righteous who run to it are exalted.
verses.18:11: The substance of a rich man is a fortified city, and its glory casts a great shadow.
verses.18:12: Before destruction the heart of a man is lifted up, and before glory it is humbled.
verses.18:13: He who answers a word before hearing, it is folly and reproach to him.
verses.18:14: A prudent servant calms the wrath of a man, but who shall endure a fainthearted man?
verses.18:15: The heart of a prudent man acquires perception, and the ears of the wise seek understanding.
verses.18:16: A man's gift enlarges him and seats him beside rulers.
verses.18:17: A righteous man is his own accuser in the opening speech; and when the adversary falls upon him, he is put to the test.
verses.18:18: A silent man puts an end to contentions, and among powers he makes decisions.
verses.18:19: A brother helped by a brother is like a fortified and lofty city, and he is strong as a firmly founded palace.
verses.18:20: From the fruits of the mouth a man fills his belly, and from the fruits of his lips he shall be filled.
verses.18:21: Death and life are in the hand of the tongue, and those who master it shall eat its fruits.
verses.18:22: He who has found a good wife has found favors and has received gladness from God; he who casts out a good wife casts out good things, and he who keeps an adulteress is foolish and ungodly.
verses.19:3: The foolishness of a man ruins his ways, yet he blames God in his heart.
verses.19:4: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor man is forsaken even by the friend he has.
verses.19:5: A false witness shall not go unpunished, and he who brings accusations unjustly shall not escape.
verses.19:6: Many court the favor of kings, but every wicked one becomes a reproach to a man.
verses.19:7: Everyone who hates a poor brother shall also be far from friendship; good insight shall draw near to those who know it, and a prudent man shall find it. He who does much evil brings wickedness to completion, and he who provokes words shall not be saved.
verses.19:8: He who acquires prudence loves himself, and he who keeps prudence shall find good things.
verses.19:9: A false witness shall not go unpunished, and whoever kindles wickedness shall perish by it.
verses.19:10: Luxury is not fitting for a fool, nor if a household servant begins to rule with insolence.
verses.19:11: A merciful man is longsuffering, and his boast comes upon transgressors.
verses.19:12: The threat of a king is like the roaring of a lion, but like dew upon the grass, so is his cheerfulness.
verses.19:13: A foolish son is a shame to a father; vows from the hire of a harlot are not pure.
verses.19:14: Fathers apportion house and possessions to children, but from God a wife is joined to a man.
verses.19:15: Cowardice holds fast an effeminate man, and the soul of an idle person shall hunger.
verses.19:16: He who keeps a commandment guards his own soul, but he who despises his own ways shall perish.
verses.19:17: He who has mercy on a poor man lends to God, and according to his gift it shall be repaid to him.
verses.19:18: Discipline your son, for thus he shall be of good hope, yet do not be lifted up in your soul to outrage.
verses.19:19: An evil-minded man shall be penalized; and if he acts wickedly, he shall add his own soul as well.
verses.19:20: Hear, son, the instruction of your father, that you may become wise in your latter days.
verses.19:21: Many thoughts are in the heart of a man, but the counsel of the Lord abides forever.
verses.19:22: Mercy is fruit to a man, and a righteous poor man is better than a lying rich man.
verses.19:23: The fear of the Lord leads to life for a man, but he who is without fear shall lodge in places where knowledge does not visit.
verses.19:24: He who hides his hands unjustly in his bosom shall by no means even bring them to his mouth.
verses.19:25: When a pestilent man is scourged, a fool becomes more shrewd; and if you reprove a prudent man, he will understand discernment.
verses.19:26: He who dishonors his father and drives away his mother shall be put to shame and become a reproach.
verses.19:27: A son who ceases to keep the instruction of a father shall meditate on evil sayings.
verses.19:28: He who becomes surety for a foolish youth mocks a righteous decree, and the mouth of the ungodly shall swallow down judgments.
verses.19:29: Scourges are prepared for the undisciplined, and punishments likewise for fools.
verses.20:1: Wine is unrestrained and strong drink is insolent, and every fool is entangled with such things.
verses.20:2: The threat of a king does not differ from the wrath of a lion, and he who provokes him sins against his own soul.
verses.20:3: It is a glory for a man to turn away from revilings, but every fool is entangled with such things.
verses.20:4: When reproached, a sluggard is not ashamed, and likewise he who borrows grain in harvest.
verses.20:5: Counsel in the heart of a man is deep water, and a prudent man shall draw it out.
verses.20:6: A great thing is a man, and a precious thing is a merciful man, yet it is a hard task to find a faithful man.
verses.20:7: He who walks blameless in righteousness shall leave his children blessed.
verses.20:8: When a righteous king sits upon a throne, no evil thing withstands before his eyes.
verses.20:9: Who will boast that he has a pure heart? Or who will boldly claim to be clean from sins? The lamp of him who speaks evil of father or mother shall be extinguished, and the pupils of his eyes shall see darkness. A portion hastily gained at the first shall not be blessed at the last. Do not say, "I will take vengeance on the enemy," but wait for the Lord, that He may help you.
verses.20:10: A great and a small weight, and double measures—both of them are unclean before the Lord;
verses.20:11: and he who makes them shall be fettered in his practices; a young man is with a devout one, and his way is straight.
verses.20:12: The ear hears and the eye sees; both of them are works of the Lord.
verses.20:13: Do not love to slander, lest you be taken away; open your eyes and be filled with bread.
verses.20:23: A double weight is an abomination to the Lord, and a deceitful balance is not good before Him.
verses.20:24: From the Lord the steps of a man are directed, but how could a mortal understand his ways?
verses.20:25: It is a snare for a man hastily to consecrate something of his own, for after vowing comes regret.
verses.20:26: A wise king is a winnower of the ungodly, and he shall bring a wheel upon them.
verses.20:27: The breath of men is a light of the Lord, who searches the inner chambers of the belly.
verses.20:28: Mercy and truth are a guard for a king, and they shall encompass his throne in righteousness.
verses.20:29: Wisdom is an ornament to young men, and gray hairs are the glory of elders.
verses.20:30: Bruises and fractures befall the wicked, and stripes into the inner chambers of the belly.
verses.21:1: As a rush of water, so is a king's heart in the hand of God; wherever He desires to turn, there He inclines it.
verses.21:2: Every man appears righteous to himself, but the Lord directs hearts.
verses.21:3: To do righteous deeds and to speak truth are more pleasing before God than the blood of sacrifices.
verses.21:4: A high-minded man is bold-hearted in insolence, and the lamp of the ungodly is sin.
verses.21:6: He who accumulates treasures by a lying tongue pursues vain things into the snares of death.
verses.21:7: Destruction shall lodge with the ungodly, for they do not desire to practice what is righteous.
verses.21:8: To the crooked God sends crooked ways, for His works are pure and upright.
verses.21:9: It is better to dwell on a corner of an open rooftop than in whitewashed rooms with unrighteousness and in a shared house.
verses.21:10: The soul of an ungodly man shall not receive mercy from any among men.
verses.21:11: When an undisciplined man is punished, the evil man becomes more shrewd; and a wise man who understands shall receive knowledge.
verses.21:12: A righteous man understands the hearts of the ungodly, and he despises the ungodly in their evils.
verses.21:13: He who stops his ears so as not to heed the weak, he also shall cry out, and there shall be no one who listens.
verses.21:14: A secret gift overturns anger, but he who withholds gifts arouses strong wrath.
verses.21:15: The gladness of the righteous practices justice, but a holy man is unclean among evildoers.
verses.21:16: A man who wanders from the way of righteousness shall rest in the assembly of giants.
verses.21:17: A needy man loves gladness, loving wine and oil for wealth.
verses.21:18: But a lawless man is the ransom for a righteous man.
verses.21:19: It is better to dwell in the wilderness than with a sharp-tongued, quarrelsome, and wrathful woman.
verses.21:20: A desirable treasure shall rest upon the mouth of a wise man, but foolish men shall swallow it up.
verses.21:21: The way of righteousness and mercy shall find life and glory.
verses.21:22: A wise man scaled fortified cities and tore down the stronghold in which the ungodly had trusted.
verses.21:23: He who guards his mouth and his tongue preserves his soul from affliction.
verses.21:24: A bold, self-willed, and boastful man is called a pestilent fellow, and he who bears a grudge is a lawless man.
verses.21:25: Desires slay a sluggard, for his hands are not willing to do anything.
verses.21:26: An ungodly man craves evil desires all the day long, but the righteous man shows mercy and compassion unsparingly.
verses.21:27: The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, for indeed they offer them lawlessly.
verses.21:28: A false witness shall perish, but an obedient man shall speak with caution.
verses.21:29: An ungodly man stands shamelessly in countenance, but the upright man himself understands his ways.
verses.21:30: There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel for the ungodly man.
verses.21:31: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, yet help comes from the Lord.
verses.22:1: A good name is more desirable than great wealth, and good favor is above silver and gold.
verses.22:2: The rich and the poor meet one another, and the Lord made them both.
verses.22:3: A shrewd man, seeing a wicked man severely punished, is himself instructed, but the foolish pass on and suffer punishment.
verses.22:4: The offspring of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and wealth, and glory, and life.
verses.22:5: Briars and snares are in crooked ways, but he who guards his own soul shall keep away from them.
verses.22:7: The rich shall rule over the poor, and household servants shall lend to their own masters.
verses.22:8: He who sows worthless things shall reap evils, and he shall complete the stroke of his works. God blesses a cheerful man and a giver, and He shall bring to an end the vanity of his works.
verses.22:9: He who shows mercy to a poor man shall himself be nourished, for he has given of his own bread to the poor. He who gives gifts gains victory and honor, yet he takes away the soul of those who possess them.
verses.22:10: Cast out a pestilent man from the council, and strife shall go out with him; for whenever he sits in the council, he dishonors all.
verses.22:11: The Lord loves holy hearts, and all the blameless are acceptable to Him; a king shepherds with his lips.
verses.22:12: And the eyes of the Lord preserve discernment, but a lawless man despises words.
verses.22:13: A sluggard makes excuses and says, "There is a lion in the roads, and murderers are in the broad streets."
verses.22:14: The mouth of a lawless man is a deep pit, and he who is hated by the Lord shall fall into it. There are evil ways before a man, and he does not love to turn away from them; yet it is necessary to turn away from a crooked and evil way.
verses.22:15: Folly is fastened to the heart of a youth, and the rod and discipline are far from him.
verses.22:16: He who oppresses a poor man multiplies his own possessions, yet he gives to a rich man only to have less.
verses.22:17: Incline your ear to the words of the wise and hear my word, and apply your heart, that you may know that they are good.
verses.22:18: And if you put them into your heart, they shall gladden you together upon your lips;
verses.22:19: so that your hope may be upon the Lord, and He may make known to you your way.
verses.22:20: And you also, write them down for yourself threefold for counsel and knowledge upon the breadth of your soul.
verses.22:21: Therefore I teach you a true word and good knowledge to heed, so as to answer words of truth to those who question you.
verses.22:22: Do not oppress a poor man by violence, for he is destitute, and do not dishonor the weak in the gates.
verses.22:23: For the Lord shall judge his cause, and you shall deliver your inviolate soul.
verses.22:24: Do not be a companion to a hot-tempered man, and do not lodge with a wrathful friend,
verses.22:25: lest you learn of his ways and take snares for your soul.
verses.22:26: Do not give yourself as surety out of deference to someone's face;
verses.22:27: for if he has nothing with which to repay, they shall take the bedding from beneath your sides.
verses.22:28: Do not move the everlasting boundaries which your fathers set.
verses.22:29: A keen-sighted man who is prompt in his works ought to stand before kings, and not stand before sluggish men.
verses.23:1: If you sit down to dine at the table of rulers, consider attentively the things set before you,
verses.23:2: and put forth your hand, knowing that you must prepare such things; yet if you are overly greedy,
verses.23:3: do not crave his delicacies, for these belong to a deceitful life.
verses.23:4: Do not measure yourself, being poor, against a rich man, but by your own understanding hold back.
verses.23:5: If you fix your eye upon him, nowhere will he alight; for wings have been fashioned for him like those of an eagle, and he returns to the house of him who presides over him.
verses.23:6: Do not dine with an envious man, nor desire his foods;
verses.23:7: for just as if someone should swallow a hair, so he eats and drinks. And do not bring him in to yourself and eat your morsel with him;
verses.23:8: for he will vomit it up and ruin your fair words.
verses.23:9: Speak nothing in the ears of a fool, lest he sneer at your discerning words.
verses.23:10: Do not move everlasting boundaries, and do not enter into the possession of orphans;
verses.23:11: for He who redeems them is the Lord; He is mighty, and He will judge their cause against you.
verses.23:12: Give your heart to instruction, and prepare your ears for words of discernment.
verses.23:13: Do not hold back from disciplining a child, for if you strike him with a rod, he will certainly not die;
verses.23:14: for you shall strike him with a rod, yet you shall deliver his soul from death.
verses.23:15: Son, if your heart becomes wise, you will gladden my heart also,
verses.23:16: and your lips will linger in words with my lips, if they are upright.
verses.23:17: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but remain in the fear of the Lord all the day.
verses.23:18: For if you keep these things, you shall have offspring, and your hope shall not depart.
verses.23:19: Listen, son, and become wise, and make straight the thoughts of your heart.
verses.23:20: Do not be a drinker of wine, nor stretch yourself out at banquets and the buying of meats;
verses.23:21: for every drunkard and fornicator shall come to poverty, and every drowsy man shall be clothed in torn and ragged garments.
verses.23:22: Listen, son, to the father who fathered you, and do not show contempt because your mother has grown old.
verses.23:24: A righteous father nurtures well, and over a wise son his soul rejoices.
verses.23:25: Let your father and mother be glad over you, and let her who bore you rejoice.
verses.23:26: Give me your heart, son, and let your eyes observe my ways.
verses.23:27: For a strange house is a pierced jar, and a strange well is narrow.
verses.23:28: For such a one shall swiftly perish, and every lawless man shall be consumed.
verses.23:29: Who has woe? Who has tumult? Who has lawsuits? And who has vexation and idle chatter? Who has bruises in vain? Whose eyes are livid?
verses.23:30: Is it not those who linger long over wines? Is it not those who seek out where drinking-bouts are held? Do not become drunk with wines, but converse with righteous men, and converse as you walk about;
verses.23:31: for if you give your eyes to the bowls and the cups, afterward you shall walk about more naked than a pestle;
verses.23:32: and at the last he is stretched out like one struck by a serpent, and as from a horned viper the venom spreads through him.
verses.23:33: When your eyes look upon a strange woman, then your mouth shall speak perverse things,
verses.23:34: and you shall lie down as in the heart of the sea, and like a helmsman in a great surge.
verses.23:35: And you shall say, "They strike me, and I felt no pain, and they mocked me, yet I did not know it. When will dawn come, that I may go and seek those with whom I may gather?"
verses.24:1: Son, do not envy evil men, nor desire to be with them;
verses.24:2: for their heart meditates on falsehoods, and their lips speak of troubles.
verses.24:3: With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it is established;
verses.24:4: with discernment storehouses are filled with all precious and fine wealth.
verses.24:5: A wise man is better than a strong man, and a man possessing prudence than a great tilled field.
verses.24:6: With guidance war is waged, and help is with a heart of counsel.
verses.24:7: Wisdom and good understanding are in the gates of the wise; the wise do not turn aside from the mouth of the Lord,
verses.24:8: but they deliberate in councils. Death meets the undisciplined,
verses.24:9: and a fool dies in sins, and uncleanness shall be stained into a pestilent man
verses.24:10: in an evil day and in a day of affliction, until he fails.
verses.24:11: Deliver those who are being led to death, and ransom those who are being slain; do not spare.
verses.24:12: But if you say, "I do not know this man," know that the Lord knows the hearts of all; and He who formed breath for all, He Himself knows all things, who renders to each according to his works.
verses.24:13: Eat honey, son, for the honeycomb is good, that your throat may be sweetened.
verses.24:14: Thus you shall perceive wisdom for your soul; for if you find it, your end shall be good, and hope shall not forsake you.
verses.24:15: Do not bring an ungodly man to the pasture of the righteous, nor be deceived by the filling of the belly.
verses.24:16: For seven times a righteous man shall fall and rise again, but the ungodly shall grow weak in evils.
verses.24:17: If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his stumbling do not be lifted up;
verses.24:18: for the Lord will see it and it will not please Him, and He will turn away His wrath from him.
verses.24:19: Do not rejoice over evildoers, nor envy sinners;
verses.24:20: for there shall certainly be no offspring for a wicked man, and the lamp of the ungodly shall be extinguished.
verses.24:21: Fear God, son, and the king, and do not disobey either of them;
verses.24:22: for suddenly they shall punish the ungodly, and who shall know the punishments of them both? A son who keeps the word shall be free from destruction, and receiving it, he has accepted it. Let no falsehood from the tongue be spoken to a king, and let no falsehood go forth from his tongue. The tongue of a king is a sword, and not of flesh; and whoever is delivered over shall be crushed. For if his wrath is sharpened, he consumes men along with their sinews, and devours the bones of men, and burns them up like a flame, so that they are inedible for the young of eagles.
verses.24:23: Now these things I speak to you who are wise, to recognize: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
verses.24:24: He who says of the ungodly, "He is righteous," shall be accursed by peoples and hated among the nations;
verses.24:25: but those who reprove shall appear better, and upon them blessing shall come.
verses.24:26: And they shall kiss lips that answer good words.
verses.24:27: Prepare your works for going forth, and make yourself ready for the field, and follow after me, and you shall rebuild your house.
verses.24:28: Do not be a false witness against your fellow citizen, nor exaggerate with your lips.
verses.24:29: Do not say, "Just as he treated me, so I will treat him, and I will repay him for the wrongs he did to me."
verses.24:30: Like a tilled field is a foolish man, and like a vineyard is a man lacking sense;
verses.24:31: if you leave him alone, he shall lie waste and become wholly overgrown with weeds, and he becomes abandoned, and his stone walls are torn down.
verses.24:32: Afterward I repented; I looked attentively to choose instruction.
verses.24:33: A little I doze, and a little I sleep, and a little I clasp my chest with my hands;
verses.24:34: but if you do this, your poverty shall come marching ahead, and your want like a good runner.
verses.25:1: These are the unarranged instructions of Solomon, which the friends of Hezekiah, king of Judea, copied out.
verses.25:2: The glory of God conceals a matter, but the glory of a king honors affairs.
verses.25:3: Heaven is high, and the earth is deep, and the heart of a king is unsearchable.
verses.25:4: Beat impure silver, and all of it shall be purified clean;
verses.25:5: slay the ungodly from the presence of a king, and his throne shall prosper in righteousness.
verses.25:6: Do not boast before a king, nor take your stand in the places of rulers;
verses.25:7: for it is better for you that it be said, "Come up to me," than that you should be humbled in the presence of a ruler. Speak the things which your eyes have seen.
verses.25:8: Do not plunge hastily into strife, lest you regret it in the end, whenever your own friend reproaches you.
verses.25:9: Withdraw backward, do not be contemptuous,
verses.25:10: lest your friend indeed reproach you, and your strife and enmity will not depart, but shall be to you equal to death. Grace and friendship deliver; guard them for yourself, lest you become subject to reproach, but keep your ways peaceably.
verses.25:11: A golden apple in a necklace of sardius, so is it to speak a word.
verses.25:12: A precious sardius is bound upon a golden earring, and a wise word into an attentive ear.
verses.25:13: As a going out in harvest during the heat brings benefit, so does a faithful messenger to those who sent him; for he benefits the souls of those who employ him.
verses.25:14: As winds and clouds and rains are most conspicuous, so is he who boasts of a false gift.
verses.25:15: In longsuffering there is prosperity for kings, and a soft tongue crushes bones.
verses.25:16: Having found honey, eat what is sufficient, lest being filled you vomit it up.
verses.25:17: Bring your foot seldom to your own friend, lest having had his fill of you he hate you.
verses.25:18: A club and a sword and a pointed arrow, so also is a man who bears false witness against his friend.
verses.25:19: The way of an evil man and the foot of a lawless man shall perish in an evil day.
verses.25:20: As vinegar is harmful to a wound, so an affliction falling upon the body grieves the heart. As a moth in a garment and a worm to wood, so the grief of a man harms the heart.
verses.25:21: If your enemy hungers, feed him; if he thirsts, give him to drink;
